requirement: Supply the test article with 8.69 g/s of air (7.38 L/s at 300 K), the mass flow implied by the existing CFD inlet condition (23.5 m/s, 20 mm bore, 300 K, 101325 Pa).
Limit the mass-flow setpoint range to the CFD-supported envelope, 90 % to 110 % of design (7.82 to 9.56 g/s), unless further CFD is run.
Control flow by blower speed. No throttling valve in the line, because a line-size valve has too little control authority at these velocities.

Derive mass flow from FE-101 differential pressure with PT-102, TT-101, PT-100 and TT-100 compensation. Proposed uncertainty at most +/-2 % of reading at the design flow, to be shown by an uncertainty budget.
Record the air temperature at IF-1 and compare it with the CFD reference of 300 K. Blower heating of about 2 to 5 K is expected (screening estimate).
Select the blower so that it delivers at least 9.41 L/s at a fan total pressure of at least 2722 Pa at full speed (the upper warm-ambient point with all-high losses is then reached at 90 % speed).

Count the CFD test-article drop exactly once, as a total-pressure loss derived from the static drop M036, and list the contraction, instrument spools and expansion separately as outside the CFD domain.
Place no valve, cap or restriction in the discharge path L-107.
Carry every component loss that lacks vendor data as a flagged assumption or allocation with a sensitivity range, and replace it with vendor data at detail design.
Set the design pressure of lines and components from the blower shut-off pressure (vendor data), or limit that pressure with PSV-101.
Keep the metering-run bore at 50 mm or more and the pipe Reynolds number at 5000 or more so the ISO 5167-2 scope is met for FE-101.
Do not restrain TA-101 axially. Accommodate the free axial growth of 1.84 mm (LC1) and up to 2.07 mm across the studied envelope, plus margin.
Use a single axial fixed point at the cold inlet end of TA-101.

Evaluate piping and connection loads on the TA-101 flanges before construction. The existing LC1 and LC2 results do not qualify the new supports, piping or connections. Full axial restraint would give about 549 kN (M091), a bounding case and not a rig configuration.
Measure the outlet bulk air temperature after mixing, with a multi-point element. A single point is not acceptable because the CFD outlet temperature is non-uniform.

requirement: Make discharge-side lines and components suitable for outlet air at the CFD bulk temperature of 368.93 K and for nearby hot surfaces. Assume no plastic.
Measure the outer-wall temperature at z = 50, 300 and 550 mm to compare with the CFD axial profile.
Define only the heater boundary. Infer no heater electrical power, wiring, construction or protection from the CFD heat flux.
Permit heater power only with proven airflow. An independent low-differential-pressure trip (PDSL-102) removes heater power through the hardwired logic ES-101.

Provide an independent over-temperature trip (TSHH-120 on its own sensor TE-120). Set it above the highest predicted normal temperature (591.13 K bound, M154) and below the material, heater and insulation limits, which are not set here.
Inhibit blower start unless HV-101 is proven open.
An emergency stop shall stop the blower and remove heater power.
After a heater shutdown, keep the airflow on until the wall temperatures fall below a limit that is set at detail design.
